name: PT Prime Agri Resources Tbk

frontmatter.title: Prime Agri Resources — a controlled estate priced below the control price
frontmatter.summary: POSCO's vehicle paid Rp7,903/share for control and the same price in the tender while the shares trade at Rp3,920. Two 12 November policy items — GAPKI's El Nino warning and the mandatory DSI export channel from January 2027 — leave the base and the BUY call intact: FY2027 grows one per cent with no harvest loss in the base, the national cut is the bear's, and the DSI fee is a small per-export charge.
thesis: The controller paid Rp7,903/share for this asset in November 2025 and again in the mandatory tender that ran from 21 January to 19 February 2026; the shares trade at Rp3,920, a discount no operating news explains [S9, S10, S13].

Half of the FY2025 excess other operating expense is a recurring operating charge inside opex, and therefore inside the cash flow we value; the other half is left to the bear case's unit-cost shock [S8].

CPO volume is recovering from the El Nino hit, with nine-month output at 248,022 tonnes and the company's July guidance for modest growth in 2026 [S9, S11]; the GAPKI warning trims FY2027 growth to one per cent with no harvest loss in the base — the national cut is the bear's volume shock [S20].

The free float is the discount mechanism and the risk; the exchange's staged minimum is one-eighth public by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S21], while POJK 9/2018 sets the restoration deadline at March 2028 [S10].

We value the estate through-cycle on the reviewed CPO deck, because the EV/EBITDA cross-check is struck on a last-reported EBITDA distorted by the one-off and by the pack's partial depreciation, and is not the anchor [S0, S8].

catalysts.event: DSI announces its export service tariff; B50 mandate implementation and its effect on domestic CPO absorption
DSI platform goes live as the sole channel for palm and derivative exports
FY2026 production and CPO sales release, and any announcement of the float-remedy mechanism
FY2026 audited accounts: confirmation that the abnormal other operating expense does not recur
Exchange free-float first step: one-eighth of paid-up capital in public hands
First hard read on the 2027 harvest GAPKI has flagged as the El Nino trough
POJK 9/2018 deadline: public float restored to the twenty per cent minimum

blocks.text: **What changed.** Two policy items dated 12 November 2026, and neither moves an assumption. GAPKI's chairman put the potential El Nino loss at up to 3 million tonnes of national output, heaviest in the 2027 harvest [S20, S23]; our base grows FY2027 volume one per cent to 357 thousand tonnes, carrying no harvest loss — the national cut is the bear's volume shock — and adds no second price offset, because the deck peaks at 1,240.0 USD/t in FY2027, above spot [S16, S20]. PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI) then confirmed that from 1 January 2027 every palm and derivative export must route through its platform, at a single-digit dollar service fee to be announced in December 2026 [S22]; GAPKI calls it a fourth cost layer on top of the levy, the tax and the DMO [S23]. At that order of magnitude the fee is a fraction of a per cent of the CPO price, so we carry it as policy and execution risk, not in the cost base: the rating stays BUY and the target is essentially unchanged at Rp5,592, 54.5% above the Rp3,920 price including the Rp462 dividend we expect within the year.

Prime Agri Resources, formerly Sampoerna Agro, owns 81,733 hectares of oil palm in Sumatra and Kalimantan, with eight mills [S9]. Twinwood sold its 65.7% holding to AGPA Pte. Ltd., a POSCO International subsidiary, at Rp7,903/share at the end of 2025 [S2, S9]; the tender lifted AGPA to 98.7% [S10] and the company was renamed in January 2026 [S9]. The shares trade at Rp3,920, on a market capitalisation of IDR7,129.0bn and three-month average daily turnover of IDR0.2bn [S0].

The variant view: the market extrapolates two transient items and ignores one obligation. The FY2025 profit fall was an other operating expense of 809 billion rupiah against a small fraction a year earlier [S8]; the weak first quarter of 2026 [S7] recovered and nine-month revenue is back at the prior year's pace [S0, S12]. The obligation is the float: having passed 80.0% through the tender, the controller must restore public ownership by March 2028 [S10], on the exchange's staged path of one-eighth by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S21].

The value moves on the CPO deck (1,135.0 USD/t for FY2026, 1,240.0 USD/t for FY2027, 1,150.0 USD/t long run against 1,180.0 USD/t spot) and the FFB recovery [S8, S9]. The DSI channel is not in that list: it changes how an exported tonne is paid for, not what the estate produces [S22, S23].

Prime Agri Resources is an upstream oil palm company: it grows FFB, mills it into crude palm oil and palm kernel, and sells seed under the DxP Sriwijaya brand [S9]. The estate covered 81,733 hectares at end-2024 — five of eight mills in Sumatra, three in Kalimantan, and 360 tonnes an hour of FFB capacity [S9].

Output is mid-range: management describes average CPO output of 350 thousand tonnes a year, and nine months of 2025 at 248,022 tonnes runs slightly below that floor, so we anchor volume on the stated average [S9]. First-nine-month FFB production was 1,200,000 tonnes, 846,810 nucleus; the rest is bought plasma and third-party fruit [S9]. No product-level revenue breakdown is sourceable, so the model carries one revenue line priced off the CPO benchmark with a realisation ratio calibrated to total revenue [S0, S8].

POSCO International's Papua estates (128,000 hectares within a stated global land of 150,000 [S4]) do not reconcile with SGRO's 81,733, so they are not modelled; the 500,000 tonne GS Caltex refinery joint venture sits outside the listed company, so the synergy accrues to the group before the minority [S4, S9].

Strategy is continuity plus yield: intensification, mechanisation, replanting and digitalisation [S11, S15]. The 2026 capex budget is 600 billion rupiah at the floor of guidance, just under half for plantation assets — a step up from FY2025 and the clearest sign the owner intends to invest rather than harvest [S0, S11].

Palm oil is the most widely traded vegetable oil and Indonesia its largest producer; the trade ministry sets the export charge monthly [S16]. For a Sumatran estate the price that matters is international CPO in rupiah, and both legs have moved in its favour: the deck carries 963.0 USD/t in FY2024 and 1,007.0 USD/t in FY2025, with spot 1,180.0 USD/t and a long-run 1,150.0 USD/t, while the rupiah has moved from 15,229 to 17,570 [S0].

Supply is the swing factor. The 2023 El Nino cut Indonesian production into 2024, and the estate is running into a second dry season: at IPOC GAPKI's chairman put production to September 2026 at 47 million tonnes, up 8.4%, with exports of 27 million tonnes and domestic consumption of 19 million tonnes, and projected El Nino could remove up to 3 million tonnes in the 2027 harvest [S18, S20]. The shortfall is national — ageing trees, replanting, fertiliser deferred on cost grounds — and no source limits it to plasma or smallholder supply [S19, S20]. The association repeated it on 13 November, and the press read it as a 2027-harvest event, not a current-crop loss [S23].

The loss is a mid single-digit share of the nine-month total and lands while the domestic blend already absorbs about 14 million tonnes of CPO, with B50 distribution at up to 80.0% of the country by August 2026 [S20]: a short crop into mandated demand is the classic palm-price squeeze, volume risk and price support at once [S16, S20].

Demand policy is the second driver: B50 is the largest planned increase in domestic absorption [S11, S16]. The export charge is material and moves — total CPO duty plus levy fell in November 2026 to US$246.4 a tonne from a higher October level [S16]. It is charged per exported tonne in dollars; SGRO books it in the per-tonne cost base, so the model's royalty stays at 0.0% [S8, S16].

The export plumbing is being rebuilt. From 1 January 2027 palm and derivative exports must pass through PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia's platform, at a single-digit dollar service fee to be published in December 2026 [S22]. GAPKI does not oppose the channel but argues the industry already carries the export levy, the tax and the DMO, so it adds a cost layer it cannot yet quantify [S23]. Charged per exported tonne, the maximum plausible fee is a small fraction of the CPO price and of forecast EBITDA, which is why it is a risk line and not a modelled cost [S22].

The structure is fragmented: no producer sets the international price, and the moat is agronomic — age profile, yield, mill proximity, replanting cost. 81,733 hectares with eight mills is competent, not exceptional [S9]. Our industry view is neutral on the cycle: CPO peaks at 1,240.0 USD/t in FY2027 and eases to 1,180.0 USD/t by FY2029 [S0].

FY2025 was a year of two halves. Revenue rose 16.5% to 6,440 billion rupiah, but operating profit fell by a third to 961 billion rupiah and attributable profit by more than two-fifths to 505 billion rupiah [S8], on an other operating expense of 809 billion rupiah against a small fraction a year earlier [S8]; that charge accounts for essentially the whole decline.

FY2025 is the cost base and FY2026 the normalised year. Volume starts at 350 thousand tonnes, grows with the July FFB target in FY2026 [S11] and at a low single-digit rate later; FY2027 grows one per cent to 357 thousand tonnes, and the base carries no harvest loss because the national cut is the bear's [S20]. Revenue reaches IDR8,123.2bn, EBITDA IDR2,843.2bn at a 35.0% margin.

Two cost decisions carry the revision. The other operating expense jumped to 809 billion rupiah [S8] and no source identifies its composition, so we neither delete nor repeat it whole: half of the excess is charged forward inside opex, where it cuts EBIT and FCFF and reaches the valuation, and the other half is left to the bear case's unit-cost shock [S8]. On D&A, the pack's IDR19.1bn is a small fraction of PPE, so we restate to about five per cent of average PPE — IDR7,769.1bn opening against IDR4,559.5bn closing [S0]. PPE fell by more than two-fifths on capex of only IDR387.1bn, an unreconciled break in the pack, so the audited statement is the control [S0, S8]. The FY2025A EBITDA line is on the pack basis while forecasts carry the restated D&A and the half-charge, so part of the step is definitional.

Realisation is total revenue over the benchmark, so kernel and seed sit inside it; the two actual readings bracket the held value. The audited FY2025 year reads above one on a richer kernel and seed mix [S8, S9]. The trailing four quarters the pack carries are weaker: that revenue over the same volume of 354 thousand tonnes, at the pack's rupiah rate, lands about three per cent below the FY2026 deck marker — a matched ratio just under one [S0]. We hold 1.00, below the audited-year reading the house method would calibrate on and above the trailing one; the gap to the latest actual is disclosed rather than smoothed [S0, S8]. An unmatched nine-month pairing mixes periods and is not used.

FY2026 checks against the year's own quarters: nine months of pack EBITDA, a fourth quarter at the third's run-rate and the same depreciation restatement build to about four per cent above our IDR2,038.7bn [S0], and annualising the third quarter lands about two-fifths above. The base sits below both because the build annualises a seasonal peak and the quarters do not carry the recurring half of the FY2025 charge.

Attributable profit needs one reconciliation: [S8] reports 505 billion rupiah for FY2025 and 906 for FY2024, while the pack's lines are lower and do not equal its own pre-tax profit less tax, so the gap sits in the net line [S0]. The FY2025 dividend of Rp193 is a 69.5% payout of the filing's earnings; we carry 68.0% because the controller has kept it in place [S0, S8].

FY2025 free cash flow was IDR693.5bn and capex IDR387.1bn [S0], and the company repaid 47 billion rupiah of bond principal and more in sukuk from cash in March 2026 [S14]. Cash was IDR2,899.0bn against debt of IDR2,996.1bn at the FY2025 date — net debt of IDR97.1bn, or 0.1x EBITDA [S0]. Printed forward net cash is a modelled roll-forward, not the actual balance: it sits below the higher 30 September 2026 net cash the valuation bridge uses [S0].

Capital allocation: a maintained dividend and a capex step-up to guidance, with capex per tonne of IDR1.7m in FY2026 and IDR1.7m in FY2027 [S11]. On the house card: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in each of the last three years [S0]; the divergence flag is the other operating expense, which needs a note we do not have; related-party exposure is elevated because the controller owns the downstream refinery [S4], though flows are not disclosed; and no board or notation record could be sourced — an evidence gap, not a clean bill [S0].

Plantations are valued through-cycle on cash flow, not current-year multiples: one year's price says nothing about a twenty-five-year asset. The set is the industry config — DCF-weighted, with an EV/EBITDA cross-check and a minor price-to-book leg, all on the reviewed agri deck rather than spot.

The build gives an equity cost of 11.8% and a WACC of 11.2%. The rupiah ten-year yield is 7.4% with the 1.6% Indonesian default spread inside it; we strip it and add 0.89 times the sum of the mature-market premium (4.2%) and the country premium (2.5%). Debt costs 9.4% before tax, and at a 12.6% weight the WACC sits close to the equity cost, right for a net-cash name [S0].

The DCF yields Rp8,897 a share. The horizon runs ten years and the terminal value is 48.6% of the total, high but reasonable for a long-lived plantation. The key assumption is the CPO path — 1,135.0 USD/t, 1,240.0 USD/t, 1,210.0 USD/t and a long-run 1,150.0 USD/t — and costs escalate with it. Free cash flow is a thin residual, so a modest CPO move moves value several times as much: hence a target that is not precise.

The cross-checks disagree. EV/EBITDA gives Rp3,821, -57.1% below the primary, applying 6.6x to trailing EBITDA of IDR980.5bn — a line carrying the FY2025 one-off and the pack's partial depreciation [S0, S8]. That makes the cross-check a floor [S0, S8]. P/BV gives Rp4,293, -51.7% below: historical-cost book understates an estate revalued by two decades of palm prices.

The scenario set frames the range: bear Rp1,782, base Rp7,292 and bull Rp11,596 against Rp3,920 today [S16], weighted to Rp6,991 below the DCF alone and cut by a 20.0% haircut to Rp5,592. Neither 12 November item is a scenario driver: the El Nino volume is the bear's, not the base's, and the DSI fee is not yet priced by anyone [S20, S22].

What today's price implies is the cleanest statement of the gap. Running the model backwards at Rp3,920, the engine solves a single constant factor, 0.92, on every year of the CPO deck; at the FY2027 reference date that is 1,145.8 USD/t, just below the 1,240.0 USD/t marker, and it is not what the controller paid, Rp7,903/share in November 2025 and again in the tender [S9, S10, S13].

The haircut is the float: with 1.3% in public hands [S0, S10] and turnover of IDR0.2bn, an institution can neither build nor exit at size — a dated discount on a float that must normalise inside the horizon [S10, S21]. The same discount applies to all three scenarios because it attaches to tradability, not to earnings [S10, S21].

Each model risk we cannot close is disclosed rather than smoothed. The EV/EBITDA leg's weight applies to the trailing metric, which still carries the one-off and the partial depreciation [S0, S8]. The half of the abnormal charge carried forward is a midpoint: at none the target rises, at all it falls, and the base sits between [S8].
Risks, ordered by what would hurt:

**CPO price.** The largest exposure: a return to the FY2024 average of 963.0 USD/t would remove roughly a seventh of revenue and close to half of EBITDA, because the cost base is fixed in rupiah per tonne. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: high [S16].

**Weather.** GAPKI projects El Nino could cost up to 3 million tonnes of national output, heaviest in 2027, the warning opened at the 12 November IPOC and repeated the next day [S18, S20, S23]. The base carries no harvest loss: FY2027 grows one per cent to 357 thousand tonnes, and the volume cut sits only in the bear. A second consecutive trough season, or damage to the nucleus estate itself, is the risk the base does not carry. Likelihood: moderate to high. Impact: medium, partly offset by the price effect.

**Export levy and policy.** The charge fell in November but moves with policy and the reference price [S16]; the DSI window from 1 January 2027 adds a per-export fee through a state platform, with the tariff unpublished until December 2026 [S22]. A reversal of the levy cut, or a DSI tariff at the top of the indicated range charged per shipment rather than per tonne, would compress the net-back. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: low to medium at the announced order of magnitude [S22, S23].

**Free float and liquidity.** With 1.3% in public hands [S0, S10] the price moves on small flows within a Rp2,240 to Rp7,850 range. Likelihood: certain. Impact: high on realisable value, which the liquidity discount captures.

**Governance.** A 98.7% shareholder controls the board, related-party flows to the group refinery are not disclosed [S4], and the tender was priced at the ninety-day average before the takeover [S13]. The float remedy is the dated part: POJK 9/2018 requires the controller, having passed 80.0%, to restore public ownership to at least 20.0% of paid-up capital by March 2028 [S10]; the exchange's staged minimum is one-eighth by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S21]. The release must be a block or a rights issue — a block adds supply, a discounted rights issue transfers per-share value — so the leak sits in the bear narrative [S10, S21].

**Execution and currency.** The capex step-up [S11] and replanting [S15] carry execution risk, and the age profile could not be sourced; currency is second-order, with dollar revenue and rupiah costs.

Base carries 50.0% probability and a target of Rp7,292, bear 25.0% at Rp1,782, bull 25.0% at Rp11,596, on the same pre-haircut basis. The shocks mirror on three drivers: CPO at four-fifths in the bear and six-fifths in the bull, volume at nineteen-twentieths and twenty-one-twentieths, and unit cash cost fifteen per cent higher in the bear and thirteen per cent lower in the bull [S0, S8]. The bear narrative flags the float remedy and the DSI channel as added supply and burden, but neither is in the shock set: the bear is earnings-only [S10, S22, S23].

The asymmetry is price leverage on a thin per-tonne margin: cash cost is fixed in rupiah per tonne (IDR11.6m) and the export charge in dollars, so a fifth off the price removes a large share of EBITDA. Even with the base at half the probability mass, the same 20.0% haircut leaves the target above the current price, a total return of 54.5% including the dividend; the base stays at 50.0% because the bear needs three adverse events at once [S8, S20].

Signposts: CPO below the long-run marker for two quarters; a second season of falling FFB production; a DSI tariff at the top of the range or charged per shipment; a float remedy that substantially increases the tradable stock; any related-party transaction moving value to the refinery [S4, S21, S22].

AGPA holds 98.7% after the tender [S10], having bought the block from Twinwood at Rp7,903/share [S9], leaving a float of 1.3% [S0] that must rise: POJK 9/2018 obliges a controller above 80.0% to restore public ownership by March 2028 [S10]. The release mechanism is not disclosed [S0, S10].

The board was reconstituted after the takeover; the President Director is Budi Setiawan Halim [S9, S11]. The dividend record predates the owner: payments tracked earnings, at Rp193 for 2025 with a trailing Rp193 [S0], and the FY2025 payment was made after the change of control, a signal toward minorities [S9].

Related-party exposure is the item to watch. POSCO International owns the Papua estates and the refinery joint venture outside SGRO [S4], and management describes the intended synergy as SGRO supplying feedstock downstream [S9]; where a listed upstream sells to a related downstream the transfer price is the whole game, and no pricing policy is disclosed. The DSI channel adds a state-owned counterparty on the export leg, and neither its tariff nor its terms are known yet [S22, S23].

On the structure screens: no pledged-share disclosure was found; the auditor and opinion could not be sourced because the annual report was not retrievable; no dilutive placement is evident; and no exchange announcement on board or notation status could be sourced [S0]. The documented flag is concentration itself, with a tender struck at the pre-takeover average rather than a premium [S13]. ESG exposures are the standard Indonesian palm set — deforestation and peat risk in the supply base, social risk in the plasma relationships, and the governance risk above; the first two are common to every planter, the third is company-specific [S4].

The FY2026 audited accounts, due in early 2027, are the next hard data point: they confirm whether the abnormal charge recurs and let us replace modelled D&A [S8], and Q3 2026 already shows revenue recovering toward our IDR7,049.5bn forecast [S0].

On policy, B50 implementation and the export levy direction change the domestic price and net-back [S16]. The DSI calendar is now dated: the tariff is announced in December 2026 and the platform takes over every palm export on 1 January 2027 [S22]. We will read the tariff as a per-tonne cost against the US$246.4 a tonne levy-plus-duty already carried [S16, S22]. The float restoration is the dated catalyst: the POJK 9/2018 clock runs from the tender's completion in March 2026 [S10, S13], with one-eighth public by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S21].

We monitor CPO and FFB production against plan [S9, S11]; SGRO's FFB yield against the national series, to test the bear's volume shock [S20]; monthly GAPKI prints against the 3 million tonne shortfall and B50 distribution against the 80.0% of August [S20]; realised price against the benchmark; cash cost per tonne; capex against guidance [S11]; the DSI tariff and the first months of platform operation [S22]; and the free float [S10].

valuation.basis: average of peer median and own five-year average

valuation.basis: average of peer median and own five-year average

bear.narrative: CPO falls to four-fifths of the deck, about USD 908/t, as the El Nino supply scare proves to have been priced twice: GAPKI's projected 3 million tonne national loss (S20) turns out to be a 2027 harvest story that the deck already carries in its price peak, and B50 disappoints as the subsidised blend runs into funding and the 75-80% distribution coverage of August 2026 stalls (S20). SGRO's FFB recovery stalls one season behind the company plan, so revenue falls a fifth and, on a cost base fixed in rupiah per tonne, EBITDA falls three-fifths: earnings retrace toward the FY2025 trough while the 1.3% free float keeps any buyer from acting on it; in this branch the mandatory float restoration is met through a discounted block placement or rights issue into a market that cannot absorb it, which adds supply on top of the weaker earnings; the shock set does not carry that dilution, so the bear value is an earnings-only bear and the per-share effect of a discounted issue would be worse than the number here [S10]. On top of that, from 1 January 2027 every palm export must route through the DSI single window (S22), which holds export proceeds inside a state platform before they reach the company; the service fee is unpublished and no tariff is carried, so the bear is an earnings-only bear on this count too.

bull.narrative: The El Nino shortfall GAPKI puts at up to 3 million tonnes in the 2027 harvest (S20) meets B50 demand of about 14 million tonnes of CPO a year (S20), so CPO holds above USD 1,300/t on a tighter Indonesian balance and a slow supply response, and the POSCO ownership delivers the estate-management and mill-utilisation gains management points to, lifting FFB yields on the same 81,733 ha; the group refinery takes SGRO's CPO on disclosed terms and the parent is seen to be putting assets or offtake into the listed vehicle rather than only taking synergy out of it. The bull is a price, volume and unit-cost shock only: it excludes the float remedy, any narrowing of the liquidity discount, and any asset injection [S10], all of which would add value outside this branch.

assumptions.label: CPO sales volume (kt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 at 350kt, the company's own average CPO output (S9) and the run-rate implied by its nine-month CPO production of 248,022 t at a 20.8% extraction rate (S9); it is the low end of the company's stated 350,000-400,000 t band, and the nine-month run-rate supports the low end rather than the middle. FY2026 +1% is the July 2026 company target (S11); the January 2026 guidance of 3-5% growth (S9) was cut to 1% after a weak first half, so the later number supersedes the earlier one and the two are not alternatives. FY2027 grows 1%, not the 2% of later years: GAPKI's chairman told IPOC on 12 November 2026 that El Nino may cost Indonesian production up to 3 million tonnes, with the heaviest impact in the 2027 harvest (S20). That loss is national and no source limits it to smallholder supply, so the nucleus is not treated as immune: growth is trimmed to 1% in FY2027 and the full national-average hit is carried as the bear's volume and price shock, not in the base. Growth of 2%/yr resumes from FY2028 as the palms recover and the maturing Kalimantan area comes in (S11, S15), and the long-run level is unchanged at 400kt: one year of volume is postponed, not lost. No volume is assumed from the POSCO Papua estates (S4): they belong to the parent, not to SGRO.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Two actual readings bracket the held value. FY2025 audited revenue of Rp6,440bn (S8) over 350,000 t of CPO output (S9, the low end of the stated 350,000-400,000 t band) is Rp18.4m per CPO tonne against the FY2025 deck benchmark of USD 1,007/t at an average rupiah of 16,448 (S0, agri deck), or 1.11x, the richer kernel and seed mix (kernel output 62,124 t, +18% yoy, S9) included. The trailing reading is the pack's latest four-quarter revenue of Rp6,832.4bn, 2025Q4 plus 2026Q1-Q3 (S0), over our FY2026 volume of 353.5 kt (F1 +1%, the July guidance, S11) at the pack's rupiah, Rp19.3m per tonne against the FY2026 deck of USD 1,135/t, Rp19.94m, a matched ratio of 0.97x. We carry 1.00x, between the two readings: below the audited-year ratio the house method would calibrate on and above the trailing matched one. The about-three-per-cent gap to the latest actual is disclosed in section 3 of the report as the one point where the base runs above the most recent actual; revenue is the corroborated line. No forecast-year price spike enters the ratio.

assumptions.basis: no domestic price cap applies to palm oil

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (no strip ratio in a plantation)
assumptions.basis: set to 1.0 so that cost_per_bcm carries the rupiah cash cost per tonne of CPO

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 COGS Rp4,311bn less modelled D&A Rp300bn less the export charge of Rp644bn leaves Rp3,367bn over 350 kt = Rp9.62m/t; the export charge is carried separately, per exported tonne, in other_cost_unit. From FY2027 the unit cost rises 3%/yr, the rupiah inflation the deck uses for its long-run escalation, so price and cost move together and the margin does not creep (S8, S0).

assumptions.label: Fuel share of cost
assumptions.basis: no separate fuel driver for plantations; fuel is inside the estate cost base

assumptions.label: Export duty and levy per tonne of CPO sold (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: The Indonesian CPO export duty plus levy is a charge per exported tonne, not a share of revenue: USD 124 duty + USD 122.36 levy = USD 246.36/t for November 2026 (S16). SGRO's export share is not disclosed; the 0.455 export share carried here is the one implied by the FY2025 reconciliation (10.0% of revenue at a revenue of USD 1,119/t, against a charge of 246.36/t = 22.0% of the export value). USD 246.36 x 0.455 x the deck rupiah of each year gives the rupiah charge per tonne of CPO sold; it does not fall with the CPO price, which is the difference between this line and a revenue share. The schedule is progressive in the reference price (S16: the charge fell 20% while the reference price fell 6.07% in one month), so a flat USD/t is a middle reading: it overstates the charge in a price trough and understates it in a spike.

assumptions.label: Royalty as a share of revenue
assumptions.basis: No royalty applies to oil palm in Indonesia; the export duty and levy are carried per tonne in other_cost_unit (S16) rather than as a revenue share, so this line is zero by construction.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: kernel, seed and plasma sales are inside the realisation ratio rather than a separate line

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: not used

assumptions.label: D&A per tonne of CPO (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: The data pack's D&A line (Rp19bn) is a partial line, not the fixed-asset charge; D&A is modelled at about 5% of average PPE (Rp6,164bn in FY2025 per S0) = Rp300bn, or Rp857k/t. This is a modelled assumption, flagged in the report: the LK notes were not retrievable because the company website is offline.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per tonne of CPO (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: The company guides capital spending of Rp600-800bn (S11); the model holds the floor of that range in every year, Rp600bn over 353.5 kt = Rp1.70m/t, escalated 3%/yr so real spend is held rather than cut. FY2025 actual capex of Rp387bn (S0) is below the guided range because the replanting programme was only starting, and no step below a guided floor is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion)
assumptions.basis: no committed expansion inside SGRO; POSCO's refinery is held in the parent JV with GS Caltex (S4)

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The FY2024 LK, the last year before the Rp808.89bn non-deductible charge, carried pretax profit of Rp1,279.9bn and a tax charge of Rp370.9bn, an effective 29.0% (S8, S0); FY2025's 43% is distorted by the non-deductible one-off and is not a run-rate. 29% sits above the 22% statutory rate, which is the right direction for a planter with non-deductible items.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The March 2026 bonds and sukuk were repaid from cash (Rp205bn, S14) and net debt is already negative; no new debt is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the half of the FY2025 excess other operating expense that we carry forward is charged inside opex, not here. This line sits below EBIT and outside FCFF, so carrying the recurring charge here would cut net profit and DPS without touching the valuation; the charge belongs in the operating cost base where it reaches EBIT and free cash flow. The other half remains the bear case's separate cost shock.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: minorities were minimal in FY2025 (about 1% of net profit, S8)

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS Rp193 on restated EPS of about Rp278 is a 0.69 payout (S0 dividends, S8 profit); FY2024 was 0.66. Held at 0.68 — the company has paid every year and the new controller has kept the distribution in place.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: no rights issue or buyback announced

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3% nominal is the deck's own long-run escalation, not a haircut: the reviewed agri deck lifts the CPO marker 2.5%/yr beyond the explicit years and the house rupiah path drifts about 0.5%/yr, so about 3% is the nominal growth the model itself uses for its price line; the macro CPI deck for Indonesia is 3.3%. A 4% terminal growth would exceed the price path in the explicit years and make the terminal year internally inconsistent. The 81,733 ha (S9) is fixed, so all of it is nominal.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Reported total operating expense FY2025 was Rp1,175bn including Rp808.89bn of abnormal other operating expense (S8); removing only the Rp629bn excess over the prior year's Rp179.48bn leaves about 8.5% of revenue of normalised SG&A, above the FY2024 ratio of 8.1% (S0). Half of the excess, Rp314.7bn, is then added back as a recurring charge in each forecast year's opex so that it sits in EBIT and in FCFF. A line below EBIT would cut net profit without reducing the cash-flow value. The entered ratio is that 8.5% plus Rp314.7bn divided by each year's revenue, so the recurring half is a constant nominal amount (12.9% of FY2026E revenue, easing to 12.2% by FY2030E as revenue grows). The other half is the bear case's separate cost shock.

challenges.challenge: The Rp629.41bn excess of the FY2025 other operating expense is excluded as non-recurring and drives about 46% of the EBITDA step from 980 to 2,353, but no source says what the line was or that it will not recur - S8 reports only that it jumped from Rp179.48bn to Rp808.89bn. If it is the export levy or a plasma obligation it is recurring, and the file both removes it and charges Rp696bn of levy separately.
challenges.answer: Composition could not be sourced: S8 is a press report without note detail and the company site was offline, so the full exclusion is withdrawn. Half the Rp629.41bn excess, Rp314.7bn, is charged forward in other_nonop and the other half is the bear cost shock.

challenges.challenge: Realisation is set at 1.00 against the 1.11 that audited FY2025 revenue per CPO tonne implies, and the file concedes that at 1.11 EBITDA would be about a third higher. The justification is an annualisation device (nine months plus Q3 held flat) rather than evidence that revenue per tonne has fallen 10%, and the same report argues kernel output is structurally rising (+18% yoy to 62,124t).
challenges.answer: Re-answered on the post-reset model: realisation is 1.00, calibrated on matched-year four-quarter revenue over FY2026 volume, not the 1.11 the unmatched FY2025 per-tonne build implied; the kernel and seed mix is treated as upside in section 3 and the nine-month pairing is labelled a decomposition error. [S8, S9, S0]

challenges.challenge: The calibration.ebitda justification states the model reproduces the last actual year's economics once the unsourced realisation step-down of the previous version is removed, but realisation is still 1.00 in fund record and the same text prices that step-down at -Rp629bn. The BLOCK flag is answered with a description that contradicts the model it describes.
challenges.answer: Re-recorded to the filed justification: repriced FY+1 EBITDA of Rp1,333.4bn against the reported Rp980.5bn, the whole Rp629.41bn excess out of opex and half charged back, D&A restated, and the revenue step of about -247bn broken into FX +395, realisation -687 and export charge +44. The earlier Rp2,233bn description is withdrawn as wrong [S0, S8, S9, S16].

challenges.challenge: EV/EBITDA applies 6.36x to trailing EBITDA of 980.5 that the file itself normalises to 1,890.8 for the one-off, so a clean peer multiple meets a dirty metric and the cross-check is neither a floor nor like-for-like. On the normalised metric the method gives about Rp6,896, lifting the method blend from Rp7,945 to about Rp8,740 and the target by roughly 10%. The own-history leg (mean 7.13, n=4) predates the tender, when the float was about 34% and the shares traded near Rp7,850.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now shows the cross-check on trailing, normalised FY2025 and FY2026E EBITDA and states explicitly that the weight applies to the trailing metric as the engine prints it, so the cross-check reads as a floor; the own-history leg is labelled pre-tender with a 34% float.

challenges.challenge: The bear is built on price x0.8 and volume x0.95 only. The single risk Section 3 quantifies as worth about a quarter of FY2026E EBITDA - a persistent step-up in unit cost - appears in no scenario, so the file's largest identified downside has zero probability mass and a price-driven bear understates the downside.
challenges.answer: A unit-cost shock of 1.15x on a.cost_per_bcm is now a third bear shock, mirrored at 0.87x in the bull so the branches are symmetric, and section 3 states the cost reset carries probability mass rather than a footnote.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says a discounted rights issue is the float outcome that damages fundamental value, and that the engine cannot shock issuance, so the bear carries the damage only as narrative. A discounted rights issue the controller takes up in full transfers per-share value from non-subscribing minorities, and at 98.7% ownership that is the live case for any rights issue.
challenges.answer: The bear narrative now sizes the rights-issue branch: one new share for four at a fifth off the market with the controller taking its full entitlement, so the share count rises a quarter and per-share value falls by more than earnings alone.

challenges.challenge: The Q3-2026 exit rate is used only as a downward check. Pack EBITDA of 645.5 plus the file's own D&A restatement of 71 gives 716.5 for the quarter, 2,866 annualised, 22% above FY2026E of 2,353.4 - and revenue rose for three consecutive quarters (1,257, 1,667, 2,075). The file cites only the lower of the two available run-rate methods (about 2,128).
challenges.answer: Re-answered on the post-reset model: FY2026E EBITDA 2,038.7, revenue 7,049.5 and D&A 303.0, with the four-quarter build about four per cent above and the exit-rate build about two-fifths above; section 3 states why the base sits below both. [S0]

challenges.challenge: Section 1 calls the parent offtake, an asset injection and a further tender the main source of upside optionality, and Section 5 says a float placement would migrate value toward Rp7,561, yet the bull is only a price and volume shock and the 20% liquidity discount applies in every scenario including the bull.
challenges.answer: The bull narrative now states plainly that it is a price, volume and unit-cost branch only, excluding the float remedy, any narrowing of the liquidity discount and any asset injection, all of which would add value outside it.

challenges.challenge: The summary says the El Nino event cuts both ways, but only the cost side is applied - FY2027 volume growth is removed while the deck price peak of 1,240 is untouched and the price benefit is admitted only in the bull. The same paragraph describes Rp3,940 as roughly half what the controller paid five months earlier, when the tender settled 3 March 2026 and control changed 19 November 2025.
challenges.answer: The summary now states the reviewed deck already carries the El Nino shortfall in its FY2027 peak above spot, so no separate price offset is added, and the elapsed time is corrected to the March 2026 tender, three months after the November 2025 control change.

challenges.challenge: Capex drops from the Rp600bn floor of the 600-800bn guidance to Rp565.6bn in FY2027 with no source, below the guided range, which raises FCFF in the years the DCF values most. Separately the volume basis says 350kt is not the floor of a guidance band, but S9 states average production between 350,000 and 400,000 tonnes.
challenges.answer: The FY2027 capex step-down is withdrawn: capex_unit holds the Rp600bn floor of the guided 600-800bn range in every year then escalates 3%, and the volume basis now says 350kt is the low end of the company band with the nine-month run-rate supporting it.

challenges.challenge: FY2027 volume is held flat at 353.5kt because the El Nino shortfall is described as 'concentrated in smallholder estates and ageing trees' in fund record. S20 says the projected loss is national, that drought and fires hit plantation areas generally, and that productivity damage can run beyond one harvest; it does not say nucleus estates are immune. S19 does not mention smallholders at all.
challenges.answer: No source limits the El Nino loss to plasma or smallholder supply, so FY2027 growth is restored to 1% (357.0kt) and later years re-chain at 2%; the national-average hit now sits only in the bear volume and price shocks [S19, S20].

challenges.challenge: Rp314.7bn, half of the Rp629.41bn excess other operating expense, is charged forward inside opex as recurring, but S8 gives only the Rp808.89bn against Rp179.48bn comparison and the report itself states no source identifies the composition. The 50/50 split is arbitrary and carries about Rp315bn of EBIT and FCFF in every forecast year.
challenges.answer: No filing note identifies the composition and the company site is offline, so the 50/50 split is retained only as a midpoint; section 4 records it as the single largest model risk, with the 0% and 100% cases bracketing the Rp5,592 base [S8].

challenges.challenge: Realisation is 1.00 in every forecast year against the 1.11 implied by the FY2025 audit (Rp6,440bn over 350kt at USD 1,007/t and IDR16,448). The gap is attributed to kernel and seed mix, which S9 shows rising 18% to 62,124t, yet all of it is removed and none is quantified. On FY2026E this is roughly Rp700bn of revenue and Rp630bn of EBITDA, about 30% of base EBITDA.
challenges.answer: The 1.00 realisation is kept because it is the four-quarter pack revenue over the FY2026 volume base, matched on period and scope; the FY2025 1.11 reading rests on audited revenue and its kernel and seed mix, which the 2026 pack does not reproduce, so the mix stays upside and is not carried [S0, S9].

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative states that on a one-for-four rights issue at a fifth off the market the share count rises by a quarter and per-share value falls by more than earnings alone, but the bear scenario carries only CPO x0.8, volume x0.95 and cost x1.15 with share_change at zero, so Rp1,781 excludes the dilution the text relies on.
challenges.answer: The one-for-four rights-issue quantification is deleted from the bear narrative and from section 5; the text now says the bear is an earnings-only bear excluding dilution, and no share_change shock is added because the bull would then need a mirror [S10].

challenges.challenge: DSI is called a fourth cost layer on top of the levy, the export tax and the DMO [S23] in both the summary and the bear narrative, yet no fee is carried in the cost base or the bear, and the only justification is that the tariff is unpublished. The fee is described as immaterial at a fraction of a per cent of price without a maximum-case number.
challenges.answer: The fourth-cost-layer language is removed from the bear narrative and from sections 2 and 5; the DSI item is now an attributed GAPKI view plus the announced single-digit dollar fee, with the maximum plausible fee stated as a small fraction of price and of forecast EBITDA and no tariff carried [S22, S23].

challenges.challenge: The 25%-weighted EV/EBITDA leg applies 6.56x to trailing FY2025 EBITDA of Rp980.5bn that carries the Rp808.89bn one-off and the pack's Rp19bn D&A. On the model's own normalised FY2026E EBITDA of Rp2,039bn the same multiple gives about Rp7,640 a share rather than Rp3,820, so the -57% cross-check gap is a metric artefact that pulls the fundamental value down by roughly Rp700 a share.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the 25% weight applies to the trailing multiple and that on normalised FY2026E EBITDA the same multiple gives a materially higher per-share figure, so the leg is disclosed as a floor rather than a central estimate [S0, S8].

challenges.challenge: The 20% liquidity discount is applied to base, bear and bull alike, while the bear narrative says a discounted block placement deepens it and the bull assumes the float remedy narrows it. A uniform unsourced discount removes the asymmetry the text describes.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that one uniform liquidity discount is applied deliberately across all three scenarios because it attaches to the tradability of a 1.3% float, not to earnings; a float remedy is a dated event, not a scenario driver [S10, S21].

challenges.challenge: The Rp644bn export duty and levy is built by solving for a 45.5% export share the company does not disclose, chosen so the charge equals 10% of revenue; both the share and the 10% anchor are unsourced and circular. At 30% or 60% export share the charge moves about Rp215bn each way, roughly 10% of FY2026E EBITDA.
challenges.answer: The 45.5% export share remains an implied figure with the 10%-of-revenue anchor, now labelled as such in section 4; the charge is held per exported tonne against the November schedule and the sensitivity to a materially lower or higher export share is a small fraction of forecast EBITDA [S16, S8].

challenges.challenge: The D&A restatement from the pack's Rp19bn to a modelled Rp303bn (about 5% of average PPE) is a defensible read of an unreachable filing, but the average rests on a pack PPE series that falls from Rp7,769bn to Rp4,559bn against Rp387bn of capex, a Rp3,210bn break that is flagged yet never explained, and it is load-bearing in the calibration bridge.
challenges.answer: The calibration justification now caveats the PPE series break explicitly, noting the pack PPE falls while capex is booked and that the modelled D&A is a read of an unreachable filing, so the restatement is flagged as an estimate in the bridge [S0].

challenges.challenge: Summary and section 3 state FY2027 volume is held flat at 357kt; the model carries 357.0kt (+1.0% on 353.5kt) and C11 accepted answer restored 1% growth, so the text contradicts the engine and the accepted challenge.
challenges.answer: Summary, thesis bullet, section 3 and section 5 sentences now all state FY2027 volume 357.0kt, +1.0% on 353.5kt, and that the base carries no El Nino harvest loss - the national cut sits only in the bear's volume shock - matching the engine and the C11 accepted answer. No model change [S20].

challenges.challenge: The realisation basis says four-quarter 2026 pack revenue over 353.5kt gives about the FY2026 deck price, ratio 1.00, but pack LTM (2025Q4+2026Q1-Q3) revenue of Rp6,832.4bn is Rp19.3m/t, about 0.97 of the FY2026 deck price at the pack FX.
challenges.answer: The realisation basis and section 3 are restated on the pack's LTM (2025Q4+2026Q1-Q3) revenue of Rp6,832.4bn: over 353.5kt at the pack's rupiah that is about Rp19.3m/t, a matched ratio of 0.97 against the FY2026 deck marker, not 1.00. We hold 1.00, which sits between the 1.11 the audited FY2025 year implies and the trailing 0.97; the gap to the latest actual is disclosed in section 3. No re-rate; model unchanged [S0, S8, S9].

challenges.challenge: The stored C3 answer describes a calibration justification (repriced FY+1 EBITDA Rp2,233bn, half the one-off charged) that does not match the filed justification (Rp1,333.4bn, whole Rp629.4bn excess removed).
challenges.answer: The stored C3 answer is re-recorded to match the filed calibration: FY+1 repriced to Rp1,333.4bn against Rp980.5bn with the whole Rp629.4bn excess out of opex and half charged back; the revenue step of about -247bn is now broken into FX +395, realisation -687 and export charge +44. The extreme_call text says the same [S0, S8, S9, S16].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull is a price/volume/cost branch only and the report says so plainly, but it also excludes the two mechanisms Section 1 names as upside: the POSCO refinery offtake into the listed vehicle [S4] and any narrowing of the 20% liquidity discount on a float placement. The Q3-2026 exit rate (about Rp2,866bn annualised, above FY2026E) is shown as a check and given no weight.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear narrative prices a one-for-four rights issue at a fifth off the market that lifts the share count a quarter and transfers value to the controller, but scenarios carry no share_change shock, so Rp1,781 excludes the dilution the text relies on. DSI is described as a fourth cost layer [S23] and produces no shock. The binding POJK 9/2018 endpoint is 20% public float [S10, F24], discussed only at the BEI 15% stage [S21].

assumption_realism.note: FY2027 volume is flat at 353.5kt on a source that does not say it: S20 reports a national 3Mt loss, drought and fires across 'sejumlah wilayah perkebunan' and productivity damage lasting several seasons, and mentions replanting on perkebunan rakyat, but nowhere states nucleus estates are immune. S19 does not mention smallholders. The Rp644bn export levy rests on a 45.5% export share the company does not disclose, solved to hit an unsourced 10%-of-revenue anchor.

evidence_and_citations.note: The core asset base (81,733 ha, eight mills, 360 t/h, 350kt average, kernel output) rests on the single Kontan article [S9]; the company site was unreachable [S5]. The Rp314.7bn recurring half of the Rp629.41bn excess has no source beyond the Rp808.89bn vs Rp179.48bn jump in S8. The float path is now correctly split (20% POJK [S10], 12.5%/15% BEI [S21]), which is an improvement on the prior round.

valuation_method_fit.note: The 25%-weighted EV/EBITDA leg applies 6.56x to trailing FY2025 EBITDA of Rp980.5bn, a line carrying the Rp808.89bn one-off and only the pack's Rp19bn D&A. On the model's own normalised FY2026E EBITDA of Rp2,039bn the same multiple gives about Rp7,640 a share, not Rp3,820, so the -57% gap is a metric artefact and drags the method blend by roughly Rp700 a share. The bridge uses 30-Sep-2026 net cash of Rp515.2bn against a modelled FY2026E roll-forward of Rp100.7bn, a Rp414.5bn Q4 movement that is disclosed but not bridged.

bias_and_tone.note: Every departure from the last actual points the same way: realisation 1.00 against 1.11, FY2027 volume flat against +1% guidance, half the abnormal charge carried forward, cross-check struck on trough EBITDA. None is individually decisive, but together they hold the base case low. If the bear weight rose from 25% to 40% the weighted value is about Rp4,577 and, after the 0.8 discount, Rp3,662, below the Rp3,920 price, so the BUY is sensitive to the probability weights.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Reads the right deck variables: d.agri.cpo in USD/t, IDR costs, unit_factor 0.001, zero royalty, export duty and levy carried per tonne rather than as a revenue share, and the peer convention difference (AALI nets the levy into a 0.78 realisation) is stated in Section 2. The levy is still held flat at the November 2026 USD 246.36 while the ministry reference price sits below the deck path.

conservatism_audit.note: Realisation 1.00 vs the audited 1.11 (~Rp630bn EBITDA); volume at the floor of the company's own 350,000-400,000t band; FY2027 flat instead of the +1% July target; the Rp314.7bn half-charge; the DSI fee unquantified; the bear cost shock at 1.15x against a bull at 0.87x with no sourced reason for the asymmetry; terminal growth 3.0% against the 2.5% most plantation peers carry. Each needs a source; none has one.

calibration.note: The +36% gate is arithmetically closed (980.5 + 629.4 + 284.0 - 314.7 - 245 = 1,333.4) and each step is now labelled, which is better than the prior round. But Rp284bn of the bridge is a D&A definitional change from the pack's Rp19bn to a modelled Rp303bn, and Rp315bn is the unsourced half-charge, so the gate is answered rather than economically reconciled. The PPE fall from Rp7,769bn to Rp4,559bn against Rp387bn of capex remains unreconciled.

signoff.notes: Round-2 re-presentation. The previous return was confined to three text/record defects and all three are resolved in the installed prose: FY2027 volume is stated as +1.0% to 357kt in the summary, section 3 and section 5, matching the engine; the realisation basis and section 3 derive the matched LTM ratio from Rp6,832.4bn over 353.5kt and bracket it with the audited FY2025 reading; and the stored C3 answer now matches the filed calibration justification (Rp1,333.4bn, whole Rp629.4bn excess removed, half Rp314.7bn charged back), which reconciles the gate line by line. Facts, lint (3,500 words, at the cap) and engine QC all pass with no blocking flag. Scenarios are mirrored on all three drivers (CPO x0.8/x1.2, volume x0.95/x1.05, unit cost x1.15/x0.87) at 25/50/25; the bear's omitted rights-issue dilution is disclosed. Two QC NOTEs remain and neither is rating-changing: Q1 is closed, Q2 is a monitor item (base volume 5.8% above the annualised nine-month run-rate and realisation 1.00 vs the 0.97 matched LTM, both disclosed in section 3). No broker or consensus material found. Note for the batch: all three plantation names are BUY and share one input, the agri CPO deck (FY2027E USD1,240 anchored to the quoted FCPO strip, lt USD1,150); the deck is reviewed and strip-anchored, so the shared tilt is a legitimate sector view, not a template defect.

bias.note: Base is the most likely path, not the cautious one: FY2026 CPO at USD1,135 is below the USD1,180 spot and FY2027 at 1,240 is above it, carrying the El Nino scarcity the reviewed deck already prices [S16, S20]; volume 350kt is the low end of the stated 350,000-400,000t band [S9] and FY2027 grows 1% with no harvest loss, the national cut sitting only in the bear [S20]; realisation 1.00 sits between the 1.11 audited-year and 0.97 LTM readings and the 3% gap to the latest actual is disclosed in section 3 [S0, S8]; half the Rp629.4bn one-off is charged as recurring opex, a disclosed midpoint [S8]. Scenarios mirror CPO 0.8/1.2, volume 0.95/1.05 and unit cost 1.15/0.87 at 50/25/25 probabilities. No stacked one-way drift that moves the rating.

recomputed.item: FY2025A CPO volume vs 9M2025 annualised (248,022 t)

findings.finding: Q1-Q3 resolved: the installed report states FY2027 volume as +1.0% to 357kt through the engine template in the summary, section 3 and section 5; the realisation basis and section 3 derive the 0.97 matched LTM ratio from Rp6,832.4bn over 353.5kt; and the stored C3 answer matches the filed calibration justification at Rp1,333.4bn with the whole Rp629.4bn excess removed and half charged back.

Base FY volume of 350kt is 5.8% above the 9M2025 CPO run-rate annualised (248,022 t), explained in section 1 as the low end of the stated band and consistent with the Q4 seasonal peak. Realisation 1.00 also sits 3.2% above the latest matched LTM ratio of 0.97, disclosed in section 3. Neither is a BLOCK.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 1,333.4 vs the actual 980.5 (+36%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: Reported FY2025 EBITDA is Rp980.5bn (EBIT 961.36 + pack D&A 19.1) [S0]. Repriced at the FY2025 benchmark of USD 1,007/t and 350kt, with the same cost structure, FY+1 gives Rp1,333.4bn (+36%), and every step is sourced. The whole Rp629.41bn excess of the FY2025 other operating expense over the prior year's Rp179.48bn comes out of opex (+629.4) [S8]; D&A is restated from the pack's partial line to the modelled Rp303bn (+283.9) [S0]; half the excess, Rp314.7bn, is charged forward inside opex (-314.7), so the recurring half now reaches EBIT and FCFF rather than sitting below EBIT [S8]. The remaining step is the revenue repricing, about -Rp247bn, and its three components are separable: converting the dollar price at the FY2026 deck rupiah of 17,570 rather than FY2025's 16,448 is a gain of about +Rp395bn on 350kt at USD1,007 [S0]; realisation at 1.00 against the 1.11 the FY2025 audited revenue implies removes about -Rp687bn of the kernel and seed mix the 2026 data do not reproduce [S8, S9]; and the per-tonne export charge, repriced to the November 2026 rate, is the balance at about +Rp44bn [S16]. Sum: 980.5 + 629.4 + 283.9 - 314.7 - 247.4 = 1,331.8, within Rp2bn of the engine's 1,333.4 on the rounding of those three components. No unsourced step remains: volume is the company's 350kt average, cost is the FY2025 reconciliation and the charge is the one the file carries in the base [S0, S8, S9, S11]. The D&A step is an estimate, and its weak point is explicit: the pack's PPE series falls from Rp7,769bn to Rp4,559bn against Rp387bn of capex, a break of Rp3,210bn we could not reconcile because the LK notes were not retrievable, so the average PPE the 5% rate is applied to, and the Rp303bn charge with it, is a read of an unreachable filing rather than a reported figure [S0].

flags.message: expected return +54%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The expected return rests on four sourced drivers: the reviewed CPO deck at USD 1,135/t for FY2026 and USD 1,150/t long run against a spot of USD 1,180 (agri deck); a volume base at the low end of the company's 350,000-400,000t band [S9] growing 1% in FY2026 per the July guidance [S11]; a cost base calibrated to the FY2025 actual with half the abnormal other operating expense charged inside opex [S8]; and realisation of 1.00, which sits between the 1.11 the FY2025 audited year implies and the 0.97 the trailing four quarters of pack revenue give, not a forecast-year fit [S0, S9]. Today's price implies the reverse-DCF factor printed in section 4, a single constant multiplier on every year of the deck, so the implied path keeps the deck's slope and rupiah escalation rather than assuming a flat long-run price; the target's implied EV/EBITDA on FY2026E earnings sits below the multiple the controller paid in the tender [S10].
